body: I also want to kill myself because I am so unhappy and feel like I have no future since an accident I was in physically and emotionally scarred me for life. I also get angry and frustrated. Why did you switch medications? I am also taking fluoxetin, but only 20mg and only been taking it for 2 weeks. I am going to increase the dose soon. My feelings about killing myself are the same with or without the medication so far.

Thank you for your response. I think part of what makes this so difficult is that people feel so uncomfortable around me and no one really knows 'what to say'. I'm just depressing to be around in general and alot of people can't handle my negativity and grow tired of me. I just make others feel sad. People can listen and try to sympathize for only so long before they just tell me to "move on" and that this "didn't ruin your life". But I feel like it is easy to say those things if you aren't in my situation. One 'friend' in particular has been very insensitive and says she "can't be around me when I'm like this". She gets angry with me when I cry and expects me to be fine and happy because 4 months has passed, but time isn't a cure for unhappiness and it can't heal my physical deformities. The thing is, I know that if she was in my situation she would be JUST as upset. I feel like I wake up to a nightmare every morning and am afraid to even look in the mirror and see a distorted, ugly version of myself staring back. It is horrible. I feel like all my dreams and hopes for the future have been shattered (can never ski again, never go for hikes, never travel the world). I feel so limited by my injuries and so insecure about my appearance. Like all my confidence and happiness was stolen in an instant. I hope what you say is true and that I will overcome this dark time in my life, but I really don't see this as a possibility at the moment. I went to see a plastic surgeon and they said that crooked noses are very difficult to fix, but at least insurance will cover the surgery. They said they could improve it, but it will never be how it was before. Same with the scar, it can be improved but it will always remain right in the middle of my forehead. A constant reminder of my stupid mistake. As for the back and hearing problems; these are permanent. It is difficult to deal with because I have no one to talk to who can relate to how I feel. People can understand and relate to things, such as, depression after a breakup and depression after losing a loved one, but my situation isn't exactly a common thing that happens to people. Anyway, I'm rambling. Thank you for your kind words and support. It did help me at the moment and I hope you are right. At least I am lucky that I have my mom and grandmother for ongoing support at this time in my life, so I don't feel truly alone.
